info.title: Slack Web API
info.description: Twelve Slack Web API methods, written by hand from the vendor method references. Read methods take query arguments, write methods a JSON body; the token, the bot token (xoxb-) of an app installed in the workspace or the user token (xoxp-) of the person who connects, is sent as Authorization: Bearer. search.messages takes a user token alone.

200.description: Every Web API answer is a JSON object whose ok says whether the call succeeded; a failure answers HTTP 200 with ok false and an error code.

get.description: Lists all channels in a Slack team.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the cursor parameter to a next_cursor attribute returned by a previous request's response_metadata. Default value fetches the first "page" of the collection.

parameters.name: exclude_archived
parameters.description: Set to true to exclude archived channels from the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return. Fewer than the requested number of items may be returned, even if the end of the list hasn't been reached. Must be an integer under 1000.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: encoded team id to list channels in, required if token belongs to org-wide app

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Mix and match channel types by providing a comma-separated list of any combination of public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im

get.description: Fetches a conversation's history of messages and events. Slack returns at most 15 messages a call to an app distributed outside the Slack Marketplace, Auto's own Slack app among them, whatever limit asks. While has_more is true, call again with cursor set to the response_metadata.next_cursor of the last answer to read the next messages.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Conversation ID to fetch history for.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the cursor parameter to a next_cursor attribute returned by a previous request's response_metadata. Default value fetches the first "page" of the collection.

parameters.name: include_all_metadata
parameters.description: Return all metadata associated with this message.

parameters.name: inclusive
parameters.description: Include messages with oldest or latest timestamps in results. Ignored unless either timestamp is specified.

parameters.name: latest
parameters.description: Only messages before this Unix timestamp will be included in results. Default is the current time.

parameters.name: oldest
parameters.description: Only messages after this Unix timestamp will be included in results.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return. Fewer than the requested number of items may be returned, even if the end of the conversation history hasn't been reached. Maximum of 999. For a new installation of an app distributed outside the Slack Marketplace, Slack answers at most 15 objects, as its changelog of 29 May 2025 says: "The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request." (https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps)

get.description: Retrieve a thread of messages posted to a conversation. Slack returns at most 15 messages a call to an app distributed outside the Slack Marketplace, Auto's own Slack app among them, whatever limit asks. While has_more is true, call again with cursor set to the response_metadata.next_cursor of the last answer to read the next messages.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Conversation ID to fetch thread from.

parameters.name: ts
parameters.description: Unique identifier of either a thread's parent message or a message in the thread. ts must be the timestamp of an existing message with 0 or more replies.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the cursor parameter to a next_cursor attribute returned by a previous request's response_metadata. Default value fetches the first "page" of the collection.

parameters.name: latest

parameters.name: oldest
parameters.description: Only messages after this Unix timestamp will be included in results.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return. Fewer than the requested number of items may be returned, even if the end of the users list hasn't been reached. For a new installation of an app distributed outside the Slack Marketplace, Slack answers at most 15 objects, as its changelog of 29 May 2025 says: "The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request." get.description: Searches for messages matching a query, in the conversations the person who connects can see. Add in:channel_name to the query to search one channel, or from:<@UserID> to find the messages of one person.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search query.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Pass the number of results you want per "page". Maximum of 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Use this when getting results with cursormark pagination. For first call send * for subsequent calls, send the value of next_cursor returned in the previous call's results

parameters.name: highlight
parameters.description: Pass a value of true to enable query highlight markers.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to return. Maximum of 100.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Return matches sorted by either score or timestamp.

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: Change sort direction to ascending (asc) or descending (desc).

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: encoded team id to search in, required if org token is used

200.description: Every Web API answer is a JSON object whose ok says whether the call succeeded; a failure answers HTTP 200 with ok false and an error code.

post.description: Sends a message to a channel.

channel.description: An encoded ID or channel name that represents a channel, private group, or IM channel to send the message to.

text.description: How this field works and whether it is required depends on other fields you use: with blocks it is the fallback string to display in notifications; without them it is the main body text of the message, plain or formatted with mrkdwn. It is not enforced as required when using blocks or attachments.

blocks.description: A JSON-based array of structured blocks.

attachments.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments.

markdown_text.description: Accepts message text formatted in markdown. This argument should not be used in conjunction with blocks or text. Limit this field to 12,000 characters.

thread_ts.description: Provide another message's ts value to make this message a reply. Avoid using a reply's ts value; use its parent instead.

reply_broadcast.description: Used in conjunction with thread_ts and indicates whether reply should be made visible to everyone in the channel or conversation. Defaults to false.

mrkdwn.description: Disable Slack markup parsing by setting to false. Enabled by default.

unfurl_links.description: Pass true to enable unfurling of primarily text-based content.

unfurl_media.description: Pass false to disable unfurling of media content.

metadata.description: JSON object with event_type and event_payload fields. Metadata you post to Slack is accessible to any app or user who is a member of that workspace.

attachments.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments.
